_notes: CALIBRATION SLICE of claude-md-guidance.json — one case, all three instruction arms, both models. 6 cells.
WHY run this before the full 24: three things are unmeasured, and all three are cheaper to learn here.

1. COST. The per-cell estimate is derived from whole-BATTERY runs (40-63 tool calls, ~20 minutes). These cases are 1-3 calls. Input tokens dominate the bill ~44:1 over output because the whole conversation is resent every step, so a short case should cost a small fraction — but nobody has measured one. This slice turns that reasoning into a number.

2. THE JUDGE. Every judge test to date drives a FAKE model. A grade is discarded unless its quote appears verbatim in the answer, and the real-world discard rate is unknown. If real judges quote loosely, the report says NOT GRADED honestly — but we would rather learn that on 6 cells than 24.
3. THE PIPELINE. Nothing in this tool has faced a real model at all.

config-investigation is the chosen case because it is the one with an objectively checkable finding (the two config files disagree about the port), so a wrong answer is unmistakable rather than a matter of taste.
Everything else is identical to the full plan, so the full run can reuse these measurements directly.
name: claude-md-guidance-calibration
